leagues.name: WTA Tour
notes: 2026 season runs 2 January to 22 November 2026; 57 tournaments per the Wikipedia 2026 WTA Tour summary (4 Grand Slams, WTA Finals, 10 WTA 1000, 17 WTA 500, 22 WTA 250, United Cup, Billie Jean King Cup qualifying round and finals). The official calendar (wtatennis.com/tournaments and api.wtatennis.com) returned HTTP 429 on every automated attempt.

The tour is branded 'WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz' from 1 January 2026 (Tennis.com, 11 Dec 2025): Mercedes-Benz is Exclusive Automobile Partner and Premier Partner, replacing Hologic as title sponsor.

PIF is a Global Partner of the WTA Tour and first-ever naming partner of the 'PIF WTA Rankings' (Tennis.com, 20 May 2024); wtatennis.com/rankings still shows 'PIF WTA Rankings' as of 25 Sep 2026, and the wtatennis.com footer lists PIF among Global Partners.

The WTA Finals left Riyadh a year early: held in Riyadh 2024 and 2025 under a three-year Saudi Tennis Federation deal; the 2026 edition is at Indian Wells (8-15 Nov 2026 per The National; the Wikipedia calendar row says the week of 9 Nov) and Charlotte, North Carolina hosts from 2027 for at least three years.
Grand Slams are run by the national federations, not the WTA; United Cup is a combined ATP/WTA event; the Billie Jean King Cup is organised by the ITF.

Shape note: tournaments are recorded as clubs (sportId tennis, leagueId wta-tour). There are no shirt kits for tournaments; kits array is empty. Tournament title sponsors and hosts are recorded in unsourced (event-host shape).

proposedRatings.reasoning: Saudi state sovereign wealth fund chaired by the crown prince; names the PIF WTA Rankings and is a WTA Tour Global Partner. State money via the Public Investment Fund: record 345 executions in 2024 and the Khashoggi assessment, plus the Evert/Navratilova criticism of the WTA's Saudi deal -> serious, with severe reserved for live armed conflict.

Abu Dhabi government sovereign wealth fund, title sponsor of two WTA 500 events (Abu Dhabi Open; DC Open 2026-2030). UAE state money: 43 activists got life sentences in the 2024 mass trial and the convictions were upheld in 2025 -> serious.
Owned by the Investment Corporation of Dubai, the Dubai government's investment arm, and owns/organises/titles the Dubai WTA 1000. Dubai state money in the UAE mass-trial context -> serious.

Abu Dhabi government body (est. 2006 under Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed) and Presenting Partner of the Mubadala Abu Dhabi Open. Direct UAE state branding on a tour event while the mass-trial convictions stand -> serious.

unsourced: Event-host facts (schema does not fit them yet), each with source: Mubadala Abu Dhabi Open (WTA 500, International Tennis Centre Zayed Sports City) is titled by Mubadala and 'presented by Abu Dhabi Sports Council', which is listed as Presenting Partner (mubadalaabudhabiopen.com, fetched 25 Sep 2026).

Event-host fact: Mubadala is sole title sponsor of the Mubadala DC Open (combined ATP/WTA 500, Washington DC, 24 Jul-2 Aug 2026) under a five-year agreement 2026-2030, after co-titling with Citi 2023-2025 (mubadala.com/en/tennis; mubadaladcopen.com).

Event-host fact: the Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships (WTA 1000 women's event, 26th edition in 2026, plus ATP 500) is 'owned and organised by Dubai Duty Free and held under the patronage of HH Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum', Ruler of Dubai (dubaidutyfreetennischampionships.com/tournament/about-the-tournament/); DDF is a holding in the Investment Corporation of Dubai's Retail & Others portfolio (web.archive.org/web/20240417164105/https://icd.gov.ae/portfolio/dubai-duty-free/), and ICD is 'the principal investment arm of the Government of Dubai' (web.archive.org/web/20240125034029/https://icd.gov.ae/about-icd/).

Event-host fact: TotalEnergies is title sponsor of the Qatar TotalEnergies Open (WTA 1000, Doha), organised by the Qatar Tennis Federation (qatartennis.org and wtaqataropen.com, which lists 'Total Energies' under 'Title sponsor'; fetched 25 Sep 2026). The rename from Qatar Total Open was not re-verified against a TotalEnergies primary source.

Event-host fact: PIF is a Premier Sponsor of the BNP Paribas Open at Indian Wells (WTA 1000 and 2026 WTA Finals venue, 8-15 Nov 2026) and describes itself as Platinum Partner of the ATP Tour, Global Partner of the WTA Tour, exclusive naming partner of the ATP and WTA Rankings, and Presenting Partner of the WTA Finals (bnpparibasopen.com/partners/pif, fetched 25 Sep 2026). The 'Presenting Partner of the WTA Finals' line likely predates the move from Riyadh and needs a date check.

Event-host fact (ended): the WTA Finals were hosted in Riyadh in 2024 and 2025 under a three-year Saudi Tennis Federation deal; the 2024 edition was the first professional women's tennis event in Saudi Arabia with a record $15.25m prize pool; the WTA requested the 2026 move and the STF accepted (The National, 1 Jul 2026). Charlotte, North Carolina hosts from 2027 for at least three years at the Spectrum Center, with the WTA investing 'alongside our partners' to fill the gap left by PIF (The National, 17 Sep 2026); SportsPro (2 Apr 2026) reported the WTA was 'set to leave Riyadh after this year', cited 'ongoing conflict in the Middle East' as adding uncertainty, and reported Saudi Arabia and PIF were 'reassessing aspects of their sports investment strategy', having already used an opt-out to end the Next Gen ATP Finals deal early (sportspro.com/news/major-events/wta-finals-saudi-arabia-riyadh-charlotte-host-april-2026/).

Player personal sponsor (does not fit club/tour records): Emirates signed Aryna Sabalenka as its first individual tennis ambassador, announced 20 Jan 2026 with an Emirates A380 tennis livery; the airline already sponsors all four Grand Slams (SportsPro, 20 Jan 2026). Emirates (rated serious in normalized/, owned by the Government of Dubai via ICD) is not a WTA Tour partner. SportsPro does not use the phrase 'official airline' for the Grand Slam deals.

Tour naming value: the $50m/year for up to 10 years Mercedes-Benz investment is a press figure reported by Tennis.com (11 Dec 2025); official terms were not disclosed. Recorded in the deal value as upTo with source.
Hologic's title sponsorship start year (2022) was not verified against a primary source; only the end (replaced by Mercedes-Benz from 1 Jan 2026) is sourced (Tennis.com, 11 Dec 2025).

PIF's tennis footprint beyond the rankings deal: PIF's tennis partnerships span events in Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid and Beijing plus the ATP Finals in Turin and the Next Gen ATP Finals (bnpparibasopen.com/partners/pif); each of those tournament-level deals needs its own verification.

Chinese events state-links: the China Open (Beijing), Wuhan Open, Ningbo Open, Guangzhou Open and Hong Kong Open are likely organised by municipal sports bodies or state-linked operators, but tournament-by-tournament ownership research was not completed in this pass (tournament sites for Wuhan and the China Open were unreachable or empty). The Billie Jean King Cup Finals are in Shenzhen, China (Sep 2026).
Chennai Open (WTA 250): its date 'isn't confirmed yet' per the Wikipedia calendar footnote (cite note 'TBC'); treat the calendar slot as provisional.

Tournament count arithmetic: Wikipedia's summary says 57 tournaments (4 GS + WTA Finals + 10 WTA 1000 + 17 WTA 500 + 22 WTA 250 = 54, plus United Cup, BJK Cup qualifying round and BJK Cup Finals = 57). The Wikipedia 2026 WTA Tour page is used as the calendar source because wtatennis.com/tournaments rate-limits automated access (HTTP 429); every one of the 57 rows was read off that page's calendar tables on 25 Sep 2026.
normalized owners.json has 'mubadala' with parentId null; its ultimate parent is the Government of Abu Dhabi (Abu Dhabi sovereign fund). Needs an update in normalized rather than the research file.
Wilson's parent (an Amer Sports brand since 1989 per amersports.com/brands/wilson/) was not traced to a controlling owner; ownerId left null.
